How do I position my baby? 
Good positioning is crucial to happy and contented breastfeeding. Not only does it ensure 
that you and your baby are comfortable, and help you avoid sore nipples, but it also helps 
the milk to flow properly and your baby to suck more efficiently. Take as much time as 
you need to make sure your baby is positioned correctly. 
CRADLE HOLD 
This is the classic breastfeeding position. Make sure your baby’s 
face and entire body are turned toward your breast—her head 
should be lying on the fleshy part of your arm. Alternatively, 
you can support her head with your opposite arm.
